doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: The can opener, cooking on the road, and never tiring of travel
summary: His father gave him a can opener; kitchenettes on the Chico tour; he now stays closer to his ailing wife.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: I’ve got a picture here of that, when we did that scene. I’ve got a picture in the book. It was strange, I’ll tell you. But it was great, and funny, when I did get married, and I told my father we got married and he gave me a can opener. He said, “here, you’re going to need this?” I said, “what are you kidding? My wife’s going to be a great cook.” Because she had never cooked before. She was a dressmaker and she used to go to work every day, and she used to come home and her mother had dinner for her see? He says to me “here. You’re going to need this.” And she says, “how dare your father, he said I was going to need a can opener?” So we went on the road, and instead of staying in hotels, there was a trombone player named Chuck Maxon with Chico Marx’s band. He and his © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

wife were married ten years, and he was old hand at being on the road. So we kind of hung out because his wife and my wife became very good friends. And she’d say, “don’t stay in the hotel,” the whole band would go in the hotel — he’d say we won’t stay in the hotel, we’ll stay in hotels with — what do they call them, kitchenettes. You know because we’re going to be in each town for a week. So rather than just spend rent money, we could cook and you’d save some money. And my wife learned how to cook that way. It was great, I loved it. It was just a fascinating story. And people ask me these questions all the time about my life on the road. When I tell them these stories, my wife says, “you’re a blabbermouth” because I never stop. I say “I can’t help it, I just love it.” I love talking about it because everybody’s fascinated by what we went through. I mean there are stories that are incredible.
Did it get to the point where you had had enough of it?

Oh until now. The only reason I don’t work as much as I did now is my wife isn’t feeling well. So I decided hey, I’ve been on the road over 50 years and she’s waiting for me all this time, now I’m going to spend some time with her, and that’s why I carry my phone with me all the time, to keep track of her. My daughter’s calling, keep track, she’s got her girlfriend sitting with her. She’s not well at all.
